- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops after peak), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply upward bias of 1–2% for first 5–7 periods.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 3–5 days, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 5-day average instead of 30-day trend.
